task: SHELFCHECK — RUNTIME CENSUS STABILITY FIX (fix/runtime-census-determinism, PR #29)
note: Goal was determinism, not a re-audit of census content. Execution order was made fully deterministic; the resulting count differs from the previously-assumed 2,542/256 baseline because that baseline itself depended on a favorable race outcome. Per instructions this was NOT forced back to 2,542 -- see deterministicIncluded/identitiesDifferingFromExpected and STOPPED_FOR_REVIEW below. Updated after PR #29 review: see lateMutationFollowUp for a second architectural gap (ownership-reconcile-v071.js could still mutate census state after the single finalization point) found during review and fixed in this revision.

before.method: 25 simulated page loads of the pre-fix (origin/main) script set, using a Node vm harness that executes the real, unmodified census-*.js files with REAL variable timers: a randomized census-data-ready delay plus a randomized per-tag execution offset for every one of the ~50 non-census <script> tags that sit between census-cleanup.js and the census-v052..059 sweep in the real index.html (modeling real fetch/parse wall-clock cost, not an immediate-execute stub). Full methodology in the PR.

cause.mechanism: Every census-mutating script (census-cleanup.js, census-v034.js, census-collapse-v035.js, census-v035-final.js, census-v040-pricing-audit.js, census-v052..059-*.js, census-v060-integrity-scrub.js, census-integrity-pass-v001.js, census-integrity-pass-v002.js, ownership-reconcile-v071.js) independently self-polled for census-data readiness (a recursive setTimeout(fn,100) retry loop) and applied its own change to `items`/`DATA.n` the instant its own poll succeeded, with no coordination between scripts. census-cleanup.js and census-collapse-v035.js hold general title-keyed EXCLUDE/COLLAPSE maps, but sit EARLIER in index.html's <script> tag order than the census-v052..059 PriceCharting sweep that ADDS new identities. Because the base census fetch (app.js's loadData(), a real async fetch+DecompressionStream) can resolve at any point relative to the ~50 intervening non-census <script> tags, whether census-cleanup.js's poll succeeds BEFORE or AFTER the sweep has added a conflicting title is timing-dependent: if cleanup runs first (its own tag's earlier position wins the race — the more frequent outcome, 14/25 runs here), it never rechecks once it has already completed, and identities the sweep adds afterward that match its own EXCLUDE map (e.g. Funko Fusion, digital-only per the map's own stated reason) are left incorrectly INCLUDED. If cleanup's retry happens to fire after the sweep (11/25 runs here, in 5 different exact counts depending on exactly which of the 11 conflict identities existed yet), it correctly excludes them. No script coordinated 'have all census-mutating scripts finished' before a general exclusion rule ran.
scriptsInvolved: app.js (loadData() — the async data-fetch every other script raced against)
census-collapse-v035.js (general COLLAPSE map — same race pattern, latent)
ownership-reconcile-v071.js (narrow ensureExcluded calls; ORIGINALLY at a very late tag position -- see lateMutationFollowUp)
census-integrity.js (non-mutating diagnostic; read the mid-load snapshot, not the final one)

fix.architecturalDescription: Replaced 15 independent poll-and-self-apply loops with a single deterministic two-phase finalization pipeline. Every census-mutating script now calls registerCensusMutation(phase, fn) (phase is 'add' or 'exclude') instead of self-polling; registration is synchronous and needs no data readiness, so it always completes in the script's own guaranteed <script>-tag document order regardless of network/fetch timing. A new census-finalize.js tag, placed after EVERY census-mutating tag (including ownership-reconcile-v071.js — see lateMutationFollowUp for why its tag was moved), awaits a real dataReady Promise (resolved once by app.js's loadData() the instant items/DATA/byId are populated — no polling) and then runs every queued 'add' function, in registration order, followed by every queued 'exclude' function, in registration order, exactly once. This guarantees every exclusion/dedup rule always sees the complete, fully-populated candidate set the add phase built, so a later-added identity can never be silently left INCLUDED just because an exclusion pass already ran before it existed. DATA.n/progress()/resetBrowse() are recomputed exactly once at the true end of the pipeline rather than after every individual script.
filesChanged: index.html (added census-finalize.js script tag; bumped ?v= cache-busting for every file above whose content changed)
fix.notChanged: No EXCLUDE/COLLAPSE/DROP/dedup rule text or eligibility logic was added, removed, or edited. No identity was manually added or removed. The only behavioral change is WHEN each already-existing rule is applied relative to the already-existing additions.

after.method: Independent Node vm harnesses (a throwaway verification script plus the checked-in tools/census-determinism-test.mjs) execute the real FIXED census + finalize scripts under the same randomized realistic timing model used for the 'before' measurement, then compare INCLUDED count, exact included-id-set (membership hash), and a SATISFIED count against a fixed synthetic ownership snapshot (every item flagged OWNED in the base data — chosen because Josh's real GameEye-derived ownership state cannot be reproduced in a stateless test session) across every run. Cross-checked against live browser page loads on the actual index.html, both before and after the PR #29 review follow-up (moving ownership-reconcile-v071.js before census-finalize.js and making late registration refuse instead of silently apply).
after.knownConflictIdentitiesRegressionCheck: All 10 sweep-added identities that match an existing EXCLUDE rule (see before.unstableIdentities, excluding the dedup-only case 2623) were EXCLUDED on every single one of the 60 runs — zero exceptions.
after.postFinalizationFreezeCheck: Added after the PR #29 review follow-up: every run also calls registerCensusMutation('exclude', fn) once AFTER census-finalize.js has already completed and asserts (a) the call throws and (b) membership is unchanged. Held on all 20 runs of the current tools/census-determinism-test.mjs (freezeHeld: true every time) — see lateMutationFollowUp.

The fix does not introduce a new opinion about these titles — it makes the codebase's OWN existing rule for them apply consistently instead of only on some loads. deterministicSatisfied (230) is measured against a synthetic 'every baseline-OWNED item' snapshot, not Josh's real GameEye-imported ownership state (256), which this stateless harness cannot reproduce; since all 10 differing identities are baseline:'NEEDED', they could not have contributed to the real 256 figure either unless Josh's own import separately matched one of them by title, which is unverified here.

lateMutationFollowUp.issueFound: PR #29 code review: census-finalize.js was positioned before ownership-reconcile-v071.js's <script> tag in index.html. Because registerCensusMutation(phase, fn) applied fn() immediately whenever censusFinalized was already true, ownership-reconcile-v071.js was still able to mutate census membership (its two ensureExcluded calls) AFTER the single finalization point had already run — undermining the 'all mutations register first -> one finalization -> membership frozen' guarantee the whole pipeline exists to provide, even though in practice its own mutations only ever excluded items and never reintroduced anything.
fixApplied: Moved the <script src="ownership-reconcile-v071.js"> tag in index.html to immediately before <script src="census-finalize.js">, right after census-integrity-pass-v002.js (real tag position 68 -> 69; census-finalize.js is now 70). Its registerCensusMutation('exclude', fn) call now registers into the normal queue like every other census-mutating script and runs as part of the single finalization pass, in the exclude phase (after every add-phase script, so its find()-by-title lookups for sweep-added titles like 'Ghost Recon: Breakpoint' still resolve correctly).

Changed registerCensusMutation() in app.js so a post-finalization call is REFUSED rather than silently applied: it now logs a console.error naming the offending phase and throws, instead of running fn() and re-rendering. Once SHELFCHECK_CENSUS_FINALIZED is set, INCLUDED/EXCLUDED membership is frozen for the rest of that page load — a misplaced <script> tag now fails loudly at load time instead of quietly reintroducing the exact class of race this pipeline exists to prevent.

tools/census-determinism-test.mjs updated to match: ownership-reconcile-v071.js moved from the old 'late/immediate-apply' special case into the normal MUTATORS list at its new tag position, and a new check added to every run that deliberately calls registerCensusMutation() after finalization and asserts it throws and leaves membership unchanged (postFinalizationFreezeCheck).
lateMutationFollowUp.verification: 20/20 regression-harness runs with freezeHeld:true (see after.postFinalizationFreezeCheck), plus 3 live browser reloads confirming ownership-reconcile-v071.js's own exclusions (Firewall Zero Hour, WWE 2K24) and its Ghost Recon: Breakpoint alias still apply correctly from the new tag position, and that a manual post-finalization registerCensusMutation() call throws with membership unchanged. INCLUDED remained 2532 throughout — the tag move and freeze enforcement are purely architectural and did not change which identities are INCLUDED.

findings: census-finalize.js (new, required for the app to finish loading at all) was absent from sw.js's offline precache list (array A) — on a fresh/offline install, the app could fail to ever finalize its census.

17 existing census-mutating files had their content changed by this fix but their index.html <script src> ?v= cache-busting query strings were left unbumped — the same class of bug found and fixed during the prior PriceCharting price-pass cleanup (PR #28): a browser that already cached the old byte content for one of these exact URL+querystring pairs would keep serving the pre-fix (racy) script indefinitely, silently defeating this fix for that user.

sw.js's own fetch handler is already network-first (cache:'no-store' live fetch, falling back to the Cache API only when the network request fails) for every GET, which independently limits staleness for an already-installed, already-online PWA — this is a secondary, not primary, freshness mechanism here.
fixApplied: Added 'census-finalize.js' to sw.js's precache array A.

Bumped sw.js's own cache-name version (shelfcheck-v120 -> shelfcheck-v121) so the browser's normal service-worker update/activate cycle purges the old precache and installs a fresh one containing the corrected files.

Bumped the ?v= query string for every one of the 17 modified census-*.js files plus app.js in index.html (all to ?v=139, one past the highest existing value on this branch) and added a new ?v=1 tag for census-finalize.js, so both a plain browser HTTP cache and a controlling service worker are forced to fetch the corrected byte content instead of serving a stale cached copy.
pwa.validation: Confirmed live: after loading index.html, navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() shows sw.js active, caches.keys() shows exactly ['shelfcheck-v121'], and that cache contains entries for both 'census-finalize.js' (from the precache list) and 'census-finalize.js?v=1' (opportunistically cached by the network-first fetch handler on first load) — confirming the new required file is available offline.
pwa.outOfScope: sw.js's precache list stores each URL WITHOUT its ?v= query string, while index.html requests the versioned URL — a pre-existing mismatch (present for all ~90 precached files before this fix, not introduced by it) that means the Cache-API offline FALLBACK path (used only when a live network fetch fails) would miss on an exact-URL match for any versioned script. This did not block the determinism fix (the network-first path already covers the common online case, and the version bump above ensures a fresh copy is fetched and re-cached under the new URL on next successful load) and was left unchanged as a separate, broader concern affecting far more than the census files touched here.
